chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the vineyard, when is its sale permissible? He said: When it sets fruit and becomes vines.

key_terms.الْكَرْم: Vineyard or land planted with grapevines
key_terms.عَقَدَ: Set fruit (specifically referring to the formation of the fruit on the plant)

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible to sell a vineyard according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific stage of fruit development required for the validity of selling produce, distinguishing between mere flowering and the formation of established fruit. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on tangible asset definition (mal) in commercial transactions, ensuring that the seller possesses a distinct, identifiable commodity at the time of sale. This ruling aligns with the broader Islamic legal principle of avoiding uncertainty (gharar) in trade by requiring the subject matter to be clearly defined and present.
